force.title: The Immigration Squeeze
force.signature: Whole industries quietly run on immigrant labor — so immigration policy and border enforcement, not wages alone, now decide who can staff the work at all.

A \u00b7 Who grows and processes the foo: Farm work depends on immigrant labor; enforcement is an existential input risk.
Meat and dairy plants run on the same labor pool — a hidden supply-chain fragility.
B \u00b7 Who builds and cleans: Construction trades are heavily immigrant-staffed; policy tightens an already-short labor market.
Cleaning, landscaping, and domestic work face the same sourcing squeeze.
C \u00b7 Who cares and who's detained: Elder and health care lean on immigrant workers just as demand surges.
Detention and vetting are the other, growing side of immigration policy.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: labor availability is set by policy, not just pay; automated or higher-wage operators cope, labor-dependent ones don't.
